kurz: Which requirements need to be checked before you buy your first individual share, from the time commitment through the statistical burden of proof and the boundary of your competence to the error log.

bloecke.md:
Active investing requires more than an opinion about the market. It is an unpaid side job whose success can only be distinguished from chance after decades, and which the German tax authorities treat less favourably than passive investing. The previous lessons described various schools, from value and momentum to countercyclical investing. None of them replaces the requirements that apply to all of them.

These requirements can be set out as a calculation with six items: time, statistical burden of proof, tax and cost hurdle, boundary of competence, position size and temperament. The calculation should be drawn up before the first purchase and repeated every year thereafter.

## Time commitment and return per hour

The effort can be quantified. The following illustrative calculation applies to a portfolio of twelve individual securities. The initial analysis of a candidate, with ten years of figures, competition, valuation and a counter-thesis, takes around twelve hours, so 36 hours for three candidates seriously examined each year. Ongoing monitoring of each position involves four quarterly statements at half an hour each and two hours for the annual report, four hours in total, or 48 hours for twelve positions. On top of that come just over 25 hours for screening, reading and evaluation. Altogether, that is around 110 hours a year, or just over two hours a week.

There is no salary for these hours. The only return is the excess return over a cheap index fund. A lead of one percentage point on €50,000 yields €500 a year before tax. The effort does not depend on the size of the portfolio, whereas the return grows with it.

bloecke.titel: Return per working hour with a lead of one percentage point and 110 hours a year
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation, before tax. The return per hour exceeds the statutory minimum wage only from a portfolio value of around €153,000, and after flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 26.375% only from around €208,000.

bloecke.md: Time is an item that investors usually leave out of the calculation, because it does not appear on the portfolio statement. 110 hours for a lead of one percentage point on €50,000 come to around €4.55 per hour. Even this amount assumes that the lead materialises at all.

## Statistical burden of proof

Excess return is a random variable. Whether a lead is based on skill or on luck cannot be read from its sign. The ratio of lead to fluctuation provides information on this: the [[Information ratio|information ratio]]. It is the average excess return divided by the [[Tracking error|tracking error]], that is, by the standard deviation of the return difference relative to the benchmark index. A private portfolio with twelve securities typically has a tracking error of ten to 15%.

An investor who is two and a half percentage points above the index over eight years, with a tracking error of 10%, arrives at an information ratio of 0.25 and a t-statistic of 0.71. This result cannot be distinguished from pure luck. Because of the multiple testing problem, Harvey, Liu and Zhu even call for a t-hurdle of 3.0 instead of 1.96. The same reasoning applies to any investor who has spent years trying out strategies.

bloecke.formel: t = IR × √T     with     IR = excess return ÷ tracking error
bloecke.erklaerung: Solving for time gives T = (t ÷ IR)². The required observation period grows quadratically as the information ratio falls.
variablen: t-statistic; from about 2, a result is conventionally considered significant
information ratio: average excess return per unit of active risk
bloecke.beispiel: With IR 0.25 and t = 2, T = (2 ÷ 0.25)² = 64 years.

bloecke.titel: Years until a lead is statistically proven
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation using T = (t ÷ IR)², assuming independent, identically distributed annual excess returns. Even a result that any professional would be satisfied with (IR 0.5) needs 16 years for the conventional threshold and 36 years for the stricter one.

bloecke.md: The U.S. Persistence Scorecard from S&P Dow Jones Indices tracks funds that were in the top quarter of their category in 2021. In the overall group of US equity funds, none of them was back in the top quarter in each of the four following years up to 2025. With pure chance, 0.25 to the power of four would have been expected, that is, 0.39%. No difference between skill and chance can be seen in these data. Among US mid caps, large caps and multi caps, too, not a single fund stayed in the top quarter over the full five years; among small caps, around 2% did.

## Taxes and costs

Individual shares have no [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)]]. Price gains on shares are subject to 25% capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) plus the solidarity surcharge, together 26.375% under the Income Tax Act (Section 32d(1) EStG, Section 20 EStG), and more with church tax. For an equity fund with an equity ratio of more than 50%, by contrast, 30% of the income remains tax-free under the Investment Tax Act (Section 20 InvStG), and the effective tax is then 18.46%. The difference of just under eight percentage points on the gain is a hurdle that comes before any selection of securities.

In addition, losses from share sales can only be offset against gains from share sales (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG). A loss on an individual security therefore does not reduce the tax on the ETF core; it is carried forward in a separate pot. However, the individual share portfolio has two advantages. There is no ongoing fund fee, and the investor decides when to realise gains. The fund investor, on the other hand, pays tax in advance in most years through the [[Advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)|advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)]] under Section 18 InvStG.

bloecke.titel: Gross return needed from individual selection for a €10,000 lump-sum investment over 20 years

bloecke.md: With the same gross return, the individual share portfolio ends up around €2,670, or just over 8%, lower after twenty years. To draw level, it needs around half a percentage point more gross return in every single year for two decades. Not taken into account are the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag, Section 20(9) EStG), the ongoing taxation of dividends and the advance lump sum. They would tend to widen the gap.

bloecke.titel: From the assumed selection advantage to the net result
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation in percentage points a year. The behaviour gap comes from Morningstar's Mind the Gap 2026 (investor return of 8.7% against a fund return of 9.9% over ten years, with a gap of more than two points for volatile funds).

bloecke.md:
## Circle of competence and its boundary

With the [[Circle of competence (Kompetenzkreis)|circle of competence]], what matters to Buffett is that you know its edge and do not cross it. The size of the circle is secondary. In practice, the circle is regularly confused with familiarity. Using a product every day says nothing about the manufacturer's capital intensity, pricing power or competitive pressure. Lynch's call to invest in what you know likewise refers to the starting point of research, not its result. The fact that at times he held over a thousand securities fits poorly with the image of the focused stock picker that is sold under his name.

The boundary can be tested with three questions that are answered in writing before the purchase.

schritte.text: Name three drivers of profit over the next five years, such as volume, price, margin or capital requirements, and state which of them is the most uncertain.
Give an explanation other than “the market is wrong”. If you cannot say what information or what patience you have that the seller lacks, you are on the wrong side when you buy.

schritte.titel: Define what would refute the thesis
schritte.text: Specify an observable event with a date, such as a margin figure, a market share or a balance sheet item. The price is not suitable, because with value approaches a falling price is normal and not a refutation.

bloecke.md:
## Position size and the Kelly criterion

The [[Kelly criterion]] determines the growth-optimal stake. In the continuous approximation for investments, it equals the expected excess return divided by the square of volatility. As a concrete number, the value is useless. As a thinking tool, it is useful because it shows how sensitively any recommendation on position size depends on the return estimate.

bloecke.erklaerung: Kelly share of a position in total wealth. The numerator is an estimate with a large error, the denominator a quantity that can be measured comparatively reliably. The result therefore changes mainly with the numerator.
bloecke.beispiel: With µ − r = 8 percentage points and σ = 35%, f* = 0.08 ÷ 0.1225 = 65% of wealth. If the true excess return is 3 points, it would be 24%. An estimation error of five points therefore shifts the “optimal” size by around 41 percentage points of the portfolio.

bloecke.md:
Two practical rules follow from this. The first is half Kelly. With half the stake, around three quarters of the growth rate is retained at half the volatility, a trade-off that is almost always right when estimates are uncertain. The second is a hard cap per position and for the active portion as a whole, regardless of conviction. Conviction is the quantity in the numerator, and it is systematically overestimated.

However, the cap also limits the benefit. If the active portion makes up 10% of wealth and delivers a lead of three percentage points, it improves the overall result by 0.3 percentage points a year. These 0.3 points have to be set against the 110 working hours.

## Temperament and the behaviour gap

A correct thesis can look like a mistake for a decade. In Kenneth French's data, even the market premium was negative in 13.5% of all rolling ten-year windows since 1926. Individual factors were in negative territory in 7 to 20% of cases even over twenty-year windows. Investors who deviate from the market therefore have to distinguish whether their thesis has been refuted or simply not yet recognised. This cannot be decided in real time.

This is where the behavioural damage arises. Morningstar's Mind the Gap 2026 puts the gap between investor return and fund return over ten years at 1.2 percentage points a year. In the calmest fifth of funds it is only 0.4 points, in the most volatile over 2.0. The more a position fluctuates, the more of its return the investor loses through their own buying and selling. Active individual selection leads, by design, to strongly fluctuating positions.

## The error log

Buffett keeps his list of mistakes in public. Dexter Shoe was paid for in 1993 with Berkshire shares worth $433 million, which were worth around $5.7 billion in 2014. The damage therefore grows with the Berkshire share price. At Tesco, hesitation after a management problem had already been recognised caused a loss of $444 million after tax; the analysis was not the mistake. Munger calls this kind of thing thumb-sucking. Buffett puts the largest item, a structural decision from 1967 and not a share, at around $100 billion.

A useful log classifies mistakes by their type and not by the size of the loss; otherwise you learn from outcomes instead of decisions.

bloecke.titel: Four types of error in the log
zeilen: The thesis was wrong because the business, margin or competition developed differently than assumed.
Name the specific assumption and add it to the checklist as a test question.
Thesis right, execution wrong, for example too large, too early, too late or at the wrong price.
Rule instead of judgement, for example a cap, a limit or a fixed date.
Recognised and not acted on. Does not appear on any portfolio statement and is therefore never evaluated.
A separate section in the log, otherwise the most expensive class of error is not recorded.
Good decision and bad outcome, or the other way round.
Change nothing. Adjusting here replaces a good rule with the memory of a single case.

bloecke.md:
## Returning to passive investing

The base rates are known. Over twenty years, 93.8% of active US equity funds lagged behind the S&P Composite 1500, and only 37.3% of the funds that existed at the start still existed at all at the end (SPIVA, June 2025). For the ten years to June 2026, Morningstar's barometer arrives at a success rate of 25% against the passive counterpart, and 11.9% for European equity managers.

There is a serious methodological critique of the SPIVA figures. In a paper from May 2026, Cremers, Fulkerson and Riley count on an asset-weighted basis, evaluate funds up to their closure and compare them with actual index funds instead of indices. For the twenty years to the end of 2024, averaged over twelve categories of US equity funds by size and investment style, they thereby arrive at 55% instead of 92% underperformance. For bond funds, the result is even reversed. The paper was funded by the Active Managers Council. That does not invalidate it, but it is part of putting it in context. Even after this correction, the majority of fund assets still lags behind on average.

bloecke.titel: Annual decision on the active portion
bloecke.unter: The horizontal axis shows whether a lead has been proven over at least five years, the vertical axis whether time and temperament are available; only in one quadrant is continuing on the previous scale justified.

felder.text: Permissible, but to be booked honestly: limited satellite, the price of learning, not retirement provision. The hours count as consumption.
Keep the cap per position and review annually. A proven lead can disappear as soon as others know about it.
Switch without hesitation: standing order, broad index fund, date in the calendar. Mathematically, this is the better solution.
An old lead is lost without ongoing maintenance. Reduce the number of positions or switch to a mechanical set of rules.

bloecke.titel: Four figures for the annual review
bloecke.md: The review takes place on a fixed date, regardless of market conditions. First, the money-weighted return of the active portion is compared with a cheap index fund for the same region, not with your own purchase price. Second, the lead in euros is divided by the hours worked. Third, you count how often one of your own rules was broken. More than two cases a year show that the problem does not lie in the selection. Fourth, you set down in writing what happens after five years without a lead, and you do so before the fifth year begins.

One to two percentage points of excess return a year over twenty years would be a very good result and yet statistically indistinguishable from luck. Investors who count on more are expecting a result that even full-time managers with teams of analysts achieve only in a small minority of cases. A second honest justification is that the active portion is the price for leaving the passive core alone. That too is a return, although it does not appear in any return calculation.

mitnehmen: The time commitment is the only item that does not appear on the portfolio statement; for twelve securities it comes to around 110 hours a year, which, with a lead of one percentage point, only pay off before tax from a portfolio value of just over €150,000.
Whether a lead is based on skill can be read from the information ratio; with IR 0.25 it takes 64 years to reach the conventional significance threshold, which is longer than an investor's lifetime.
No partial exemption under Section 20 InvStG applies to individual shares, so compared with an equity ETF they need around 0.4 percentage points more return after costs a year just to draw level.

Above all, the Kelly criterion shows how strongly any position size depends on the return estimate; half Kelly delivers three quarters of the growth at half the volatility and is supplemented by a hard cap.
The error log must separate analysis, execution, omission and chance cases, because if you only note losses, you learn from outcomes instead of decisions.
Returning to the index follows from four figures that you write down once a year, and it is not a defeat.

begriffe.text: Average excess return over a benchmark index, divided by the tracking error. It measures how much lead is achieved per unit of active risk and thus determines how long it takes before skill can be distinguished from luck.
Standard deviation of the return difference between a portfolio and its benchmark index. A private portfolio with around a dozen individual securities typically lies at ten to 15% a year.

The area in which an investor can reliably assess a business model. According to Buffett, the key is to know the edge of this area precisely; its size is secondary. Familiarity with a product does not establish a circle of competence.

Rule for the growth-optimal stake. For investments, it corresponds approximately to the expected excess return divided by the square of volatility. In practice, only a fraction of it is used, because the result reacts very sensitively to errors in the return estimate.

A judgement that was recognised but not acted on, where no purchase or sale was made despite the reasoning being in place. The error does not appear on any portfolio statement and is therefore not recorded without a separate section in the log.
